section13_checks.prohibition_description: Treating Grant Agreement Annex templates as the governing structural schema for proposal writing.
Inventing call constraints, scope requirements, expected outcomes, or expected impacts not present in Tier 2B.
Inventing project facts (partners, capabilities, roles, objectives, budget figures) not present in Tier 3.
Commencing any Phase 8 activity before the budget gate (Phase 7) has passed.
Storing durable decisions only in agent memory without writing them to Tier 4.
Allowing a workflow or skill to become a de facto constitutional authority.
Silently reordering phases or weakening gate conditions when inputs are incomplete.
Finalizing proposal text when source state is incomplete, contradictory, or unvalidated without flagging the gap.
Using agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe rules as a substitute for reading Tier 1 documents.
Producing Tier 5 outputs not traceable to specific inputs in Tier 1–4.
Modifying Tier 1 or Tier 2 source documents to reflect project-specific assumptions.
Treating CLAUDE.md as advisory or optional.

check_notes.13.1: No structural reference to any 'Annex [0-9]', 'Grant Agreement Annex', 'AGA Template', or 'Model Grant Agreement template' is used as a schema authority. Findings are structured against MSCA-PF evaluation criteria (Excellence, Impact, Quality and efficiency of the implementation) — the correct Tier 2A/2B evaluation framework, not annex structure.
check_notes.13.2: Criterion and sub-criterion references (e.g. 'Quality of the supervision, training and of the two-way transfer of knowledge', 'the extent to which they go beyond the state of the art') are the standard MSCA-PF evaluation framework against which the review is conducted; they are not invented call constraints. The review-packet artifact type (orch.tier5.review_packet.v1) carries no per-claim traceability_footer field; no fabricated call requirement is asserted.
check_notes.13.3: Named project facts (Dr. Roland Hollós as research associate, AgroVIR, Miklós Maróti, HUN-REN ATK, ELTE, MATE, Krumatic, person-month figures ATK 2.5 / ELTE 2.0 / AgroVIR 3.0 / MATE 2.4 / Krumatic 1.5, fellow's 30 PM) appear only inside 'evidence' fields as quotations FROM the excellence/impact/implementation sections under review, not as fresh assertions by the review packet. No new project fact is fabricated; the artifact is a derived review artifact grounded in the reviewed Tier 5 sections. Conservative application confirms no fabrication.
check_notes.13.4: Artifact is a Phase 8 (orch.tier5.*) review artifact. The TAPM input boundary for this skill permits reading only CLAUDE.md and artifact_path, so phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json could not be independently re-verified here. No budget-gate contradiction was found in the audited content: person-month references are review-evidence quotes, and several are explicitly flagged by the packet itself as unconfirmed/assumed pending written confirmation (F-5, F-8), while the fellow's 30 PM is described as 'confirmed' — consistent with a completed unit-cost derivation (§8.1) and a passed gate_09. No budget figure is asserted as a newly confirmed value by the packet. Pass recorded without fabricating verification of the gate; independent gate re-verification is out of this skill's input scope and is the scheduler's responsibility.
check_notes.13.5: Not checkable from artifact content alone; enforced by decision-log-update skill. Recorded pass per skill spec.
check_notes.13.6: Not checkable from an artifact; structurally non-applicable. Recorded pass per skill spec.
check_notes.13.7: Phase 8 artifact references only same-or-prior-phase section outputs (excellence, impact, implementation); no reference to a higher-numbered phase's outputs as inputs. No silent reordering detected.
check_notes.13.8: The review packet does not finalize proposal text; it is an audit artifact. Furthermore it actively flags incomplete/unvalidated source state rather than papering over it (F-5, F-7, F-8 flag items 'declared assumed pending written confirmation'), which is constitutionally aligned with §13.8's intent.
check_notes.13.9: No Tier 1 regulatory claims (participation conditions, grant agreement terms, financial regulation) are asserted; content is confined to evaluation-criterion judgments. No generic-programme-knowledge substitution for Tier 1 detected.
check_notes.13.10: Every finding is anchored to a section_id and quotes 'evidence' drawn from the reviewed Tier 5 sections, providing traceability appropriate to a review-packet artifact type (which carries no formal traceability_footer field). Content is derivable from the Tier 5 sections under review, themselves derived from Tier 1–4. No untraceable claim detected.
